advances: A sub-sharp obstruction for the specified residual-centroid selector and the endpoint fibers in one actual body.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The coordinates and volumes are exactly those of 0fcb7fa715e2af62. That fact proves the actual three-fiber census, $D\subset B\cap\{x_1\le r\}$, $1/32<m<(11/20)^5<1$, $|C|=V$, $0<a<10^{-5}$, $(A+C)/2=D$, and the stated exact $H_1$ mass and strict bound. In particular every admissible removal has mass at most $mV<V$, so its residual has a centroid in $B$.

For positive removal write $t=\eta(B)/V$ and let $g_\eta$ be its centroid. The first moment of the original simplex is $V g_B$ with $(g_B)_1=1/6$. By subtracting the removed first moment and dividing by the remaining mass,
$$
y_\eta=\frac{g_B-t g_\eta}{1-t},\qquad
(y_\eta)_1-\frac16=\frac{t}{1-t}\left(\frac16-(g_\eta)_1\right)>0.
$$
The strict sign holds because $(g_\eta)_1\le r<1/6$. Zero removal gives $g_B$, with equality at $1/6$. All these marks at base zero lie in $H_1$, since its threshold is $1/6-(2/25)a<1/6$. Convexity of the halfspace includes their entire convex hull. The family includes subtraction of ordinary volume on $D=(A+C)/2$ and any dominated output supported there. For the ordinary removal, $D$ has one vertex of first coordinate zero and five of first coordinate $r$, so $(g_D)_1=5r/6$ and the displayed residual excess equals $103m/[3600(1-m)]$.

At each endpoint mark choose a largest barycentric coordinate in its five-simplex. Its value is at least $1/6$, so the containing simplex vertex cap is a homothetic simplex of relative volume at most $(1-1/6)^5$. Extend the affine margin of this own-fiber cap by a multiple of the base coordinate minus the endpoint base. Choose the sign toward the endpoint and large enough magnitude to exclude all other bounded fibers strictly. Thus the original raw depth is bounded by $\Gamma_5$ times the own volume there. Both endpoint bounds are strictly below $\Gamma_5 M/2$ since $0<a<1$. The largest of these two upper bounds and $\mu(H_1)$ is a fixed strict upper bound on raw depth over the specified union. Divide by $M$.

statement:
Let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^5:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$ have volume $V=1/120$. Set $r=497/3000$, $\ell=11/12-(9/2)r$, and $T=3979/6000$. Let $D$ be the simplex with vertices $(0,11/12,0,0,0)$, $b_0=(r,\ell,0,0,0)$, and $b_0+T e_i$ for $i=2,3,4,5$. Put $m=|D|/V$, $q=m^{-1/5}$, $A=(2-q)D$, $C=qD$, and $a=|A|/V$. Take the lifted convex hull with $A,B,C$ at bases $-1,0,1$. These are the three actual fibers, with masses $aV,V,V$ and $0<a<10^{-5}$. Let $\mu$ denote their summed original five-volume, $M=(2+a)V$, and $\Gamma_5=(5/6)^5$.

For every $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_B\,dx$ supported on $D$, including $\eta=0$, let $y_\eta$ be the true centroid of $\mathbf 1_B\,dx-\eta$. The convex hull of all $(0,y_\eta)$ is contained in the single closed cap
$$
H_1=\{(z,x):x_1+(1-q)rz\ge1/6-(2/25)a\},\qquad
\mu(H_1)=V\Gamma_5[1+(12/125)a]^5<\Gamma_5 M/2.
$$
Each point of the endpoint fibers has raw depth at most $V\Gamma_5 a$ at $-1$ and $V\Gamma_5$ at $1$. Consequently there is a uniform normalized depth bound strictly below $\Gamma_5/2$ on the union of the residual-centroid convex hull and the two endpoint fibers.
title: One fixed cap covers every midpoint-supported residual centroid
